title.narrative: Cities Driving Growth: Strengthening Municipal Collaboration for Economic Development

description.narrative:
The initiative is a pilot effort to strengthen collaboration and peer learning between Mozambique’s major municipalities and to test whether more structured city-to-city cooperation can create practical value and be sustained over time. The pilot combines national municipal exchange with an international port-city learning component.
As a first step, mayors and senior municipal officials from Maputo, Beira, Chimoio, Nampula, and Quelimane will participate in a peer-learning workshop in Maputo focused on practical municipal governance challenges. Municipalities will exchange experiences on revenue generation, land administration, taxpayer databases, digitalization, and service delivery, with the aim of identifying approaches and solutions that can be adapted and replicated across cities.
The pilot also includes a four-day port-city learning exchange in the Netherlands, involving representatives from the Ministry of Transport and Logistics, CFM, ANAMM, and the municipalities of Maputo, Beira, and Nacala. Through visits and meetings in Rotterdam and Vlissingen, participants will engage with Dutch municipalities, port authorities, and private sector actors to exchange experiences on port governance, port-city cooperation, urban planning linked to port development, and economic corridor development.
The pilot builds on ANAMM’s coordination role and draws inspiration from Dutch municipal cooperation models supported by VNG International. Rather than immediately establishing a formal platform, the initiative is designed to test the value of regular municipal exchange and institutional collaboration and to assess the potential for a more structured platform for collaboration between Mozambique’s major cities in the future
